messages.subject: Changing Sampler Assignment Rules
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I am just getting into using nimble so forgive me if this has an obvious answer. I am using nimble to run open population spatial capture recapture models and I am struggling with setting up the samplers for stochastic nodes. My model consists of 4 years of data where individual animal activity centers are designated within a discrete statespace. When I use configureMCMC() it defaults to assigning a different sampler to year 1 (posterior predictive) than for years 2-4 (RW) for the stochastic node that assigns these activity centers. All the other node samplers are correct. What is the best way to do this?

I tried using the code outlined on the help page for samplerAssignmentRules function and addRule, but R does not recognize the function. 
my_rules <- samplerAssignmentRules(empty = TRUE)
Error in samplerAssignmentRules(empty = TRUE) : 
  could not find function "samplerAssignmentRules"

I also looked at the nimbleOptions and it gave me this for the sampler assignment rules section:
$MCMCdefaultSamplerAssignmentRules
[[1]]
Error in cat(x, ..., sep = sep) : 
  argument 1 (type 'S4') cannot be handled by 'cat'

I appreciate any guidance on this!
Best
Colby

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Changing Sampler Assignment Rules
parts:
Colby, thanks so much for your use of NIMBLE, and also posting this question to our list.

The short answer is that the samplerAssignmentRules is a slick way of setting "new rules" for how NIMBLE assigns its default samplers (to the different nodes / dimensions of your model).  That said, for a more practical approach, I'm going to recommend you simply modify the samplers yourself, using the methods of the MCMC configuration (conf) object.  This will be more straightforward and transparent.  e.g.,

## create conf object, and see the default sampler assignments
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = TRUE)

## remove all samplers acting on any component of "sxy" variable
conf$removeSamplers("sxy")

## add a specific type of sampler (say "RW") to all nodes in nodeNames vector
for(n in nodeNames) {
    conf$addSampler(type = "RW", target = n)
}

The process for creating the nodeNames vector can be automated, as well.  We can help with that, if you're able to share more details of your model (either on, or off-list).

And, if your animal activity centers are restricted on a discrete statespace, as you mentioned, then RW Metropolis-Hastings samplers might not be the right choice - in fact, they wouldn't work.  But perhaps I'm not understanding the model setup.

And finally, if the MCMC is assigning posterior_predictive samplers to any set of nodes, then it's because they have no (stochastic) dependencies, and that is, in fact, the best choice sampler for them.  Is there any chance the model definition isn't quite right?  I'm just guessing, though, it's hard to say without seeing the model.

Cheers!  Happy Friday!

Daniel

parts:
Thanks for the great answer Daniel!

I would not consider myself a bayes pro so there is the possibility of  an issue with my model formulation. I am using 2 different methods for the point process of assigning activity centers to individuals. The first is the standard method using a uniform/dcat distribution across the study area/statespace; however, since my sampling occurred over multiple years, each individual, i, is given a new activity center each year, t. Since the statespace is not a perfect rectangle, I use a vector of of pixel IDs (nPix) to assign si to a pixel center. probability values(s.probs) associated with each pixel in the statespace.
for(i in 1:M){
  for(t in 1:Year){
    # independent activity centers for each year
    activ.s[i,t] ~ dunif(1,  nPix)        # This is for an irregularly shaped Statespace, s.probs=1 for all pixels
    s.x[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,2],round(activ.s[i,t]))    # easting of activity center from mask pixel
    s.y[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,3],round(activ.s[i,t]))    # northing of activity center from mask pixel
  }
myCalculation <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(grid = double(1), index = double()) {  ## index could be int() but model variables are represented as double anyway
    return(grid[index])
    returnType(double(0))
  })

For the second method, the code is similar, but the s.probs vector relates to values from a previously computed resource selection function with values associated to each pixel in the statespace, this is an inhomogenous point process:
    activ.s[i,t] ~ dcat(s.probs[1:nPix])         # inhomogenous point process for activity centers with RSF likelihood
    s[i,t,1] <- myCalculation(Mask[,2],activ.s[i,t])    # easting of activity center from mask pixel
    s[i,t,2] <- myCalculation(Mask[,3],activ.s[i,t])    # northing of activity center from mask pixel

Even though the plotting of activity centers for all 4 years is the same, the configureMCMC assigns a different sampler to the first year, ie activ.s[i,1]. What sampler would you recommend for this?

I implemented the code you provided in the previous post, which seems to work. Although I'm not sure how the second part gets used. Before taking away any samplers, the getSamplers() returns
[[10]]
posterior_predictive sampler: activ.s[1, 1]
[[11]]
RW sampler: activ.s[1, 2]
[[12]]
RW sampler: activ.s[1, 3]
[[13]]
RW sampler: activ.s[1, 4]
[[14]]
posterior_predictive sampler: activ.s[2, 1]

....and so on to activ.s[180,4]

How do I keep this format when changing just the nodes activ.s[i,1] to a different sampler?

Thanks so much for your help! Happy Friday to you as well!

Colby

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Changing Sampler Assignment Rules
parts:
Good questions all around, Colby.  And it sounds like an interesting ecological problem you have.

Short answer, either way you have it would work, technically.  But by nature of how the sampling would work in the first dunif parameterization (activ.s[i,t] ~ dunif(1,  nPix)), I think in practice it would fail pretty hard, since M-H sampling will generally work better with "well-behaved" distributions, eg. ideally unimodal, whereas here, since the probabilities you describe in s.probs could induce any such posterior over this space, I think you're better with the second option you gave, the dcat parameterization.  (even the first way, without using s.probs and using the uniform distribution, I suppose it would work fine, but still feels less natural to me).  So I'm going to suggest the second, but encourage you to try both, and compare results.

On another note, I'll recommend you use conf$printSamplers(), rather than conf$getSamplers().  The getSamplers() method has an important place sometimes, but it's intended more for *programatic* manipulation of the conf object.  It's main role is to *return* a list with all the configuration information - not to print that information nicely for you, which is the primary function of printSamplers.

Finally, as for your questions about how to assign / remove samplers, just take a look at the short example I put together, below.  Hopefully it will answer your questions.

Hope this helps!  Keep in touch!  Thanks for using NIMBLE.

library(nimble)

code <- nimbleCode({

for(i in 1:M) {
        for(t in 1:Year) {

##activ.s[i,t] ~ dunif(1,  nPix)
            ##s.x[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,2],round(activ.s[i,t]))
            ##s.y[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,3],round(activ.s[i,t]))
activ.s[i,t] ~ dcat(s.probs[1:nPix])
s[i,t,1] <- myCalculation(Mask[,2], activ.s[i,t])

s[i,t,2] <- myCalculation(Mask[,3], activ.s[i,t])
        }
    }
})

myCalculation <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(grid = double(1), index = double()) {

return(grid[index])
    returnType(double(0))
})

M <- 180
Year <- 4
nPix <- 1000
s.probs <- rep(1/nPix, nPix)   ## uniform probabilities
Mask <- array(0, c(nPix, 3))   ## I know that 0's don't make sense here

constants <- list(M=M, Year=Year, nPix=nPix, s.probs=s.probs, Mask=Mask)

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants)  ## you probably want data and inits also

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

conf$printSamplers()

## if you see posterior_predictive samplers assigned,
## again it's because nothing in your model (in particular:
## no latent states, nor any data) *depend* on those
## nodes.  So the MCMC simply takes draws from their
## prior distribution to sample them, because in that
## case, prior = posterior.

## Anyway, let's remove whatever samplers were assigned,
## and I'd recommend either 'categorial' samplers,
## which could be slow but will sample well, or 'slice' samplers

## In response to this question:
## How do I keep this format when changing just the nodes activ.s[i,1] to a different sampler?
sNodes <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames(paste0('activ.s[1:',M,',1]'))
conf$removeSamplers(sNodes)

## this next scalarComponents = TRUE is a very new feature,
## just added within the past month or so.  tbh I'm not
## sure if it made the most recent release or not (?)
## so let me know if it doesn't work:
conf$addSampler(target = sNodes, type = 'slice', scalarComponents = TRUE)

## to change samplers on *all* the 'activ.s' nodes,
## say to the other option of categorical samplers:
sNodesAll <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames('activ.s')
conf$removeSamplers(sNodesAll)
conf$addSampler(target = sNodesAll, type = 'categorical', scalarComponents = TRUE)

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
... compile, run, etc....

## remove all samplers acting on any component of "sxy" variable

## to change samplers on *all* the 'activ.s' nodes,

}

On Friday, October 18, 2019 at 8:26:37 AM UTC-6, Daniel Turek wrote:
Colby, thanks so much for your use of NIMBLE, and also posting this question to our list.

The short answer is that the samplerAssignmentRules is a slick way of setting "new rules" for how NIMBLE assigns its default samplers (to the different nodes / dimensions of your model).  That said, for a more practical approach, I'm going to recommend you simply modify the samplers yourself, using the methods of the MCMC configuration (conf) object.  This will be more straightforward and transparent.  e.g.,

## create conf object, and see the default sampler assignments
conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, print = TRUE)

## remove all samplers acting on any component of "sxy" variable
conf$removeSamplers("sxy")

## add a specific type of sampler (say "RW") to all nodes in nodeNames vector
for(n in nodeNames) {
    conf$addSampler(type = "RW", target = n)
}

The process for creating the nodeNames vector can be automated, as well.  We can help with that, if you're able to share more details of your model (either on, or off-list).

And, if your animal activity centers are restricted on a discrete statespace, as you mentioned, then RW Metropolis-Hastings samplers might not be the right choice - in fact, they wouldn't work.  But perhaps I'm not understanding the model setup.

And finally, if the MCMC is assigning posterior_predictive samplers to any set of nodes, then it's because they have no (stochastic) dependencies, and that is, in fact, the best choice sampler for them.  Is there any chance the model definition isn't quite right?  I'm just guessing, though, it's hard to say without seeing the model.

Cheers!  Happy Friday!

Daniel

On Saturday, October 19, 2019 at 12:54:28 AM UTC-6, Daniel Turek wrote:
Good questions all around, Colby.  And it sounds like an interesting ecological problem you have.

Short answer, either way you have it would work, technically.  But by nature of how the sampling would work in the first dunif parameterization (activ.s[i,t] ~ dunif(1,  nPix)), I think in practice it would fail pretty hard, since M-H sampling will generally work better with "well-behaved" distributions, eg. ideally unimodal, whereas here, since the probabilities you describe in s.probs could induce any such posterior over this space, I think you're better with the second option you gave, the dcat parameterization.  (even the first way, without using s.probs and using the uniform distribution, I suppose it would work fine, but still feels less natural to me).  So I'm going to suggest the second, but encourage you to try both, and compare results.

On another note, I'll recommend you use conf$printSamplers(), rather than conf$getSamplers().  The getSamplers() method has an important place sometimes, but it's intended more for *programatic* manipulation of the conf object.  It's main role is to *return* a list with all the configuration information - not to print that information nicely for you, which is the primary function of printSamplers.

Finally, as for your questions about how to assign / remove samplers, just take a look at the short example I put together, below.  Hopefully it will answer your questions.

Hope this helps!  Keep in touch!  Thanks for using NIMBLE.

library(nimble)

code <- nimbleCode({
    for(i in 1:M) {
        for(t in 1:Year) {
            ##activ.s[i,t] ~ dunif(1,  nPix)
            ##s.x[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,2],round(activ.s[i,t]))
            ##s.y[i,t] <-  myCalculation(Mask[,3],round(activ.s[i,t]))
            activ.s[i,t] ~ dcat(s.probs[1:nPix])
            s[i,t,1] <- myCalculation(Mask[,2], activ.s[i,t])
            s[i,t,2] <- myCalculation(Mask[,3], activ.s[i,t])
        }
    }
})

myCalculation <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(grid = double(1), index = double()) {
    return(grid[index])
    returnType(double(0))
})

M <- 180
Year <- 4
nPix <- 1000
s.probs <- rep(1/nPix, nPix)   ## uniform probabilities
Mask <- array(0, c(nPix, 3))   ## I know that 0's don't make sense here

constants <- list(M=M, Year=Year, nPix=nPix, s.probs=s.probs, Mask=Mask)

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants)  ## you probably want data and inits also

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

conf$printSamplers()

## if you see posterior_predictive samplers assigned,
## again it's because nothing in your model (in particular:
## no latent states, nor any data) *depend* on those
## nodes.  So the MCMC simply takes draws from their
## prior distribution to sample them, because in that
## case, prior = posterior.

## Anyway, let's remove whatever samplers were assigned,
## and I'd recommend either 'categorial' samplers,
## which could be slow but will sample well, or 'slice' samplers

## In response to this question:
## How do I keep this format when changing just the nodes activ.s[i,1] to a different sampler?
sNodes <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames(paste0('activ.s[1:',M,',1]'))
conf$removeSamplers(sNodes)

## this next scalarComponents = TRUE is a very new feature,
## just added within the past month or so.  tbh I'm not
## sure if it made the most recent release or not (?)
## so let me know if it doesn't work:
conf$addSampler(target = sNodes, type = 'slice', scalarComponents = TRUE)

## to change samplers on *all* the 'activ.s' nodes,
## say to the other option of categorical samplers:
sNodesAll <- Rmodel$expandNodeNames('activ.s')
conf$removeSamplers(sNodesAll)
conf$addSampler(target = sNodesAll, type = 'categorical', scalarComponents = TRUE)

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
... compile, run, etc....
